title: 5 Site Factors That Increase VCT Top-Scrub and Recoat Quotes: Obstacles, Soil Load, Escorts and Furniture Moves
seoTitle: VCT Scrub and Recoat Quote Factors: Obstacles, Soil Load & Access
metaDescription: VCT scrub-and-recoat quotes rise 15%–45% from obstacles, soil load, escorts and furniture moves. See the uplift math, then compare bids in the Comparator.
excerpt: A VCT top-scrub and recoat that prices at $0.18–$0.35 per sq ft on an empty corridor can climb 15%–45% once furniture, heavy soil, security escorts and phased access enter the scope. This guide shows office managers which site conditions drive each uplift and how to shrink them before the walkthrough.
quickAnswer: Most US vendors price a VCT top-scrub and recoat (machine scrub with a maroon or blue pad, rinse, then two coats of finish) at roughly $0.18–$0.35 per sq ft of hard floor on a clear, moderately soiled floor. Five site factors push that number up: obstacle density, furniture-moving labor, after-hours security escorts, heavy soil or worn finish, and phased or segmented access. Combined, they typically add 15%–45% to the base estimate, so a $1,320 job on 6,000 sq ft can land anywhere from about $1,520 to $1,915.

blocks.text: What a Base VCT Scrub-and-Recoat Quote Assumes

Every scrub-and-recoat estimate starts from an idealized floor: open square footage, light-to-moderate soil, an existing finish that is intact enough to bond with new coats, and a crew that can walk in, set cones and work straight through. Under those conditions an experienced two-person crew with a 17- or 20-inch low-speed machine, an auto-scrubber or wet vac, and a finish applicator can scrub, rinse and lay two coats on roughly 4,000–6,000 sq ft per shift. That productivity is what produces the familiar $0.18–$0.35 per sq ft range seen on national bids.

The problem is that very few occupied offices look like that idealized floor. Cubicle pedestals, chair mats, copier stations, server-room ramps and breakroom tables all break up the machine path. Grit tracked from parking garages grinds the finish down to bare tile in traffic lanes. Building management may require a guard to unlock suites after 7 p.m. Each of these conditions converts into labor hours, and labor is 60%–75% of any floor project price. At a specialty floor-care rate of $55–$95 per technician hour, an extra three crew-hours adds $165–$285 before any material.
The Five Factors and What They Add

The table below uses a 6,000 sq ft VCT area quoted at a base of $0.22 per sq ft, or $1,320, as the reference job. The percentage ranges reflect how mid-market US floor contractors typically build uplifts into a written proposal. They overlap in practice, which is why the combined total usually lands between 15% and 45% rather than the simple sum.

blocks.caption: Typical uplift on a $1,320 base VCT scrub-and-recoat (6,000 sq ft at $0.22/sq ft)
rows: More than one fixed or heavy item per 100 sq ft; edge-heavy private offices

blocks.text: A floor machine covers open floor quickly, but edges, corners and the gaps around fixed furniture are hand-scrubbed with a doodlebug pad or edging tool. Private-office layouts with 10x12 rooms can be 30%–40% edge by area, compared with 10% in an open corridor. Estimators count fixed obstacles such as built-in reception desks, copier stands bolted to the floor, bollards and floor boxes, because each one forces a slow pass and extra finish feathering so the coats do not puddle against the base. Expect the bid to rise 10%–20% when obstacle density is high.
Factor 2: Soil Load and Existing Finish Condition

A top-scrub only removes the upper layers of finish and embedded soil. When traffic lanes have worn through to bare tile, the contractor must scrub harder, apply a sealer or an extra coat in those lanes, and sometimes spot-strip. Sticky residue from neutral cleaners used at the wrong dilution, or quaternary disinfectant film left by daily mopping, keeps new finish from bonding and leads to peeling within weeks. Contractors who see black lanes, powdering finish or heavy heel marks add 10%–25%, and some will refuse to warrant a recoat and recommend a full strip at $0.35–$0.75 per sq ft instead.

blocks.title: When a recoat is the wrong job
blocks.text: If more than about a quarter of the floor shows bare tile, a scrub-and-recoat will look good for a month and then fail. Ask the bidder to state in writing whether the existing finish can accept new coats, and price a strip-and-refinish alternate so you are not paying for a recoat twice.

Moving and resetting furniture is the most underestimated line in floor proposals. A typical workstation has a mobile pedestal, a task chair, a chair mat, power strips and a trash can. Two technicians can clear and reset roughly 12–20 workstations per hour, so a 40-seat floor can eat two to three crew-hours just in moves. Contracts that say furniture by others push that work back to your facilities team. Contracts that say light furniture only usually exclude desks, file cabinets over two drawers and anything with a monitor arm. Clarify which applies, and photograph the space before the crew arrives to avoid damage disputes.
Factor 4: After-Hours Escorts and Building Access

Class A and multi-tenant buildings often require a security guard or building engineer to unlock suites, operate freight elevators and stay on site while outside vendors work. Some landlords bill the escort directly to the tenant at $35–$65 per hour; others expect the floor contractor to absorb wait time. Either way, a crew that waits 30 minutes for a guard at the start of a shift loses one full room of production. Vendors add 5%–12% when the building requires escorts, freight elevator reservations or a certificate of insurance naming both landlord and property manager as additional insureds.

Finish needs 30–45 minutes between coats and several hours before heavy traffic. When a tenant cannot vacate a whole floor, the contractor splits the job across nights, which repeats setup, cone placement, chemical mixing and cleanup. Areas that run around the clock, such as security desks, data rooms or a 24/7 call center, must be done in small segments with traffic diverted. Each additional mobilization typically costs the equivalent of the $90–$135 per-visit minimum many vendors apply, which is why phasing adds 5%–12% to the total.
How to Cut the Uplifts Before the Walkthrough

items.name: Measure hard floor separately
items.text: Give bidders the VCT square footage only, net of carpet, so the base rate is applied to the right number and no one pads the takeoff.

items.name: Pre-clear the small items
items.text: Have staff lift chair mats, trash cans, boxes and floor-level cords the afternoon of the job. That alone can remove 30–60 minutes of crew time.

items.name: Fix daily soil sources
items.text: Correct mop-chemical dilution, stop disinfectant residue on floors, and place entrance matting so the recoat lasts. Restroom dispensers that drip or spill paper add soil next to doorways.

items.name: Book escorts and elevators in advance
items.text: Reserve the freight elevator and guard coverage for the full shift and share the confirmation with the contractor so no wait time is billed.

items.name: Consolidate access windows
items.text: Offer one weekend window instead of three weeknights whenever the tenant can tolerate it, eliminating repeat mobilizations.

blocks.text: Restroom-adjacent corridors are a recurring trouble spot. Touchless roll-towel dispensers such as the Georgia-Pacific enMotion 10-inch unit, with its infrared sensor and ADA-compliant depth, and the non-proprietary San Jamar Tear-N-Dry Essence, which runs on four D-cells and takes universal 8-inch rolls, cut the wet paper litter that gets ground into VCT outside restroom doors. A high-capacity Tork Twin Jumbo T2 tissue dispenser with stub-roll feed reduces run-outs that lead occupants to track water while hunting for paper. These are small changes, but they lower the soil load the next scrub has to fight.

faqs.q: How much does a VCT scrub-and-recoat cost per square foot?
faqs.a: Expect roughly $0.18–$0.35 per sq ft of hard floor for a clear, moderately soiled area with two coats of finish. Heavy soil, worn finish, furniture moves, escorts and phased access can add 15%–45%. Amortized across a whole building that mixes carpet and VCT, a quarterly floor program usually works out to about $0.03–$0.06 per sq ft per month.

faqs.q: Should furniture moving be included in a recoat quote?
faqs.a: Only if the proposal says so explicitly. Many contracts include light furniture such as chairs, mats and small tables, and exclude desks, loaded file cabinets and anything with electronics. Ask for a written scope exclusion list and a per-hour rate for additional moves, usually billed at the $55–$95 specialty floor-care rate.

faqs.q: What insurance and safety documents should a floor contractor provide?
faqs.a: Request a certificate of insurance showing general liability and workers compensation, with your company and the landlord named as additional insureds if the lease requires it. Floor strippers and finishes fall under OSHA Hazard Communication, so the crew should carry Safety Data Sheets on site and use proper eye and skin protection. If you have green purchasing goals, ask for Green Seal GS-40 certified finishes and cleaners.

faqs.q: How does a quarterly recoat show up in a monthly cleaning budget?
faqs.a: Divide the annual cost by 12. For example, four recoats a year on 6,000 sq ft at $1,500 each total $6,000, or $500 per month. Compare that with nightly service billed on 4.33 weeks per month so you are adding monthly figures on the same basis.

faqs.q: Can better daily cleaning delay the next scrub-and-recoat?
faqs.a: Yes. Dust mopping before damp mopping, using neutral-pH cleaner at the label dilution, keeping disinfectant residue off finished floors, and maintaining 10–15 feet of entrance matting can stretch a recoat cycle from quarterly to semiannual in low-traffic suites, roughly halving the annual floor-care spend.
